title: Wisdom Wiki of Methodologies : Way To Success
description: A knowledge base dedicated to systematically introducing, explaining, and applying various powerful methodologies, helping people on their path to success.

items.title: Agile ROI Calculator
items.content_html: A free calculator that estimates the annual cost of a team's meeting time and the savings from more efficient agile ceremonies. Includes the formula, assumptions, a worked example and what the number does and doesn't tell you.

items.title: Hybrid Project Management
items.content_html: A practical playbook for projects that mix agile execution with waterfall governance. Learn when hybrid makes sense, how to map epics to milestones, run a weekly interface sync, manage buffers, and avoid water-scrum-fall.

items.title: ESG Reporting
items.content_html: ESG reporting discloses a company's environmental, social and governance performance and risks. Learn what ESG covers, single vs double materiality, the main frameworks and standards (GRI, ISSB/SASB, TCFD, ESRS), greenhouse gas scopes, implementation steps and common pitfalls.

items.title: DevOps
items.content_html: DevOps unites development and operations to deliver software faster and more reliably; DevSecOps builds security into every stage. Learn the CALMS principles, the DevOps lifecycle, core practices like CI/CD and infrastructure as code, the four DORA metrics and common pitfalls.

items.title: Mixed Methods Research
items.content_html: Mixed methods research combines quantitative and qualitative data in one study to get a fuller answer than either alone. Learn the core designs (convergent, explanatory sequential, exploratory sequential), how to integrate results, a planning template and common mistakes.

items.title: Qualitative Research
items.content_html: Qualitative research explores experiences, meanings and processes through interviews, observation and texts. Learn the main methods, sample sizes, how to ensure rigor, an interview guide template, how it differs from quantitative research, and common mistakes.

items.title: Quantitative Research
items.content_html: Quantitative research collects numerical data and uses statistics to describe, find relationships and test hypotheses. Learn the main designs, the research process, sampling and measurement basics, a study plan template, how it compares with qualitative research and common mistakes.

items.title: Cornell Note Taking
items.content_html: The Cornell note-taking method divides a page into notes, cues and a summary to turn passive notes into active review. Get the page layout and template, the 5 R's process, examples for lectures, meetings and books, digital tips and common mistakes.

items.title: Feynman Technique
items.content_html: The Feynman Technique tests real understanding by explaining a concept in plain language. Learn the 4 steps, when to use it, a ready-to-use learning card template, worked examples and the 6 most common mistakes.

items.title: First Principles Thinking
items.content_html: First principles thinking breaks a problem down to basic facts and rebuilds the solution from there. Learn how it differs from reasoning by analogy, a 3-step method, Musk's rocket and battery examples, a template and when not to use it.

items.title: Pyramid Principle
items.content_html: Barbara Minto's Pyramid Principle teaches you to lead with the conclusion and support it with grouped, logically ordered arguments. Learn the four rules, the SCQA opening, before-and-after examples, a template and common mistakes.

items.title: Correlational Research
items.content_html: Correlational research measures how strongly two or more variables are related without manipulating them. Learn how to interpret correlation coefficients, the main types and methods, why correlation is not causation, a planning template and common mistakes.

items.title: Descriptive Research
items.content_html: Descriptive research systematically describes what is happening in a population or phenomenon: who, what, when, where and how much. Learn the main methods (surveys, observation, case studies), a design template, how it differs from correlational and experimental research, and common mistakes.

items.title: Experimental Research
items.content_html: Experimental research tests cause and effect by manipulating an independent variable and controlling other factors, ideally with random assignment. Learn the main designs, a planning template, threats to validity, how A/B tests fit in, and common mistakes.

items.title: Iceberg Model
items.content_html: The Iceberg Model is a systems thinking tool that looks beneath visible events to patterns, underlying structures and mental models. Learn the four levels, guiding questions, a worksheet, examples and where leverage for change really lies.

items.title: System Dynamics
items.content_html: System dynamics models how complex systems behave over time through stocks, flows, feedback loops and delays. Learn the core concepts, how to draw causal loop diagrams, common system archetypes, examples like the bullwhip effect, and common modeling mistakes.

items.title: Action Research
items.content_html: Action research combines taking action and studying it in repeated cycles of plan, act, observe and reflect, usually with the people affected. Learn the cycle, a planning template, examples in education and organizations, quality criteria and common mistakes.

items.title: Grounded Theory
items.content_html: Grounded theory builds theory from qualitative data through open, axial and selective coding, constant comparison and theoretical sampling. Learn the steps, the main schools, a coding example, a memo template and common mistakes.

items.title: SBI Feedback Model
items.content_html: The SBI model (Situation-Behavior-Impact) helps you give specific, non-judgmental feedback. Learn the steps, the SBII extension, ready-to-use scripts, upward feedback examples and the mistakes to avoid.
